summary.text: Executive summary defining digital health, explaining the rationale for updating the 2018 classification into the three-axis Classification of Digital Interventions, Services and Applications in Health (CDISAH), and summarizing the structural updates—most notably replacing Systems Categories with restructured Services and Application Types.

sections.extract: Executive Summary Digital health is the systematic application of information and communications technologies, computer science, and data to support informed decision-making by individuals, the health workforce, and health systems, to strengthen resilience to disease and improve health and wellness.(1) The pace of innovation in digital health is rapid and constant, with new interventions being developed,

sections.title: Page 8

summary.text: Summarizes the major content changes in the second edition—shifting from 'Client(s)' to 'Person(s)' or 'Individual(s)', adding pandemic-era and emerging DHIs, expanding descriptors and synonyms, and organizing Services and Application Types into five architectural representations—accompanied by the complete classification overview chart.

sections.extract: The major content changes to this edition of the Classification include: » “Client(s)” are now referred to as “Person(s)” or “Individual(s)” to maintain a more neutral terminology when referring to individuals who access health interventions from the health system.​ » Where possible, the language is updated to ensure the DHIs are inclusive of healthcare systems that have a variety of policies and models for

sections.title: Page 9

summary.text: Introduces the purpose and audience of the Classification of Digital Interventions, Services and Applications in Health (CDISAH), reviews the four foundational use cases that motivated the first edition alongside technical standards (COBIT, HL7, ISO), and lists ten current global applications of the classification.

sections.extract: What is the Classification of digital interventions, services and applications in health? The classification of Digital Interventions, Services and Applications in Health (DISAH) categorizes the different ways in which digital and mobile technologies are being used to support individuals and health system needs. It acknowledges the diverse ways in which digital capabilities are leveraged in different digital

sections.title: Page 10

summary.text: Explains how the CDISAH is organized across its three axes—nine Health System Challenge categories, four primary-user DHI groupings (Persons, Healthcare Providers, Health Management and Support Personnel, and Data Services) with synonyms and examples, and five architectural representations of Services and Application Types—and introduces how to use them together.

sections.extract: The Health System Challenge framework provides an overview of needs and challenges faced in health systems that reduce optimal performance. They describe overarching problems faced by health systems which can be addressed through implementing digital health interventions. sections.extract: SERVICES AND APPLICATION TYPES The digital services and application types represent the types of software, information and communications technology (ICT) systems and services or communication channels that deliver or execute the digital health intervention(s) and health content.
